inputs.name: MaxIterations / MaxIter
inputs.notes: The selected solver decodes the exact nonnegative structural count and requires it to fit the selected solver's structural count (u32 for the conic adapters, usize for fmincon and fminunc); zero is honored.

integer_capabilities.notes: The selected linprog, lsqlin, quadprog, fmincon or fminunc option extension is checked independently of model data.

inputs.name: OptimalityTolerance / TolFun and ConstraintTolerance / TolCon
inputs.notes: The selected lsqlin or quadprog profile requires positive finite tolerances exactly representable as binary64.

integer_capabilities.notes: No new integer model-data or solver-form support is implied.

inputs.name: MaxNodes and MaxFeasiblePoints
inputs.notes: Structural limits retain exact addressable values and must fit usize; zero/Inf admission follows the selected intlinprog profile.

integer_capabilities.notes: Counts remain actual node relaxations and certified feasible point discoveries.

inputs.name: AbsoluteGapTolerance, RelativeGapTolerance, ConstraintTolerance, MaxTime and ObjectiveCutOff
inputs.notes: Non-count integer controls cross the existing exact binary64 scalar boundary and retain their individual range checks.

integer_capabilities.notes: This does not change model data-class or variable-domain semantics.

inputs.name: count, bandwidth, flag or sparsity-pattern option value
inputs.notes: Typed iteration/evaluation/PCG/node/feasible-point counts and finite bandwidths are RunMat-only controls checked exactly against the platform size range and published in their native signed/unsigned class; scalar integer arrays normalize to native scalars. Typed flags are checked as 0/1 before logical publication. Native integer HessPattern carriers retain their class/storage; the model owner validates their pattern meaning.

integer_capabilities.notes: Counts use exact integer-to-usize parsing and retain native class; 0/1 controls become logical fields. Ordinary floating/default count values remain double. This describes RunMat count/publication behavior, not unverified MATLAB integer-overload parity; RunMat returns a struct rather than MATLAB's options object.
